Present: Mr. Yashveer Kharb, Advocate
 for the petitioner.

[1]. At the very outset, learned counsel for the petitioner very fairly submits that with respect to
inadequacy of compensation granted to the petitioner-
petitioner Trust in terms of the Award dated 30.06.2020, the statutory remedy of invoking
arbitration is available to the petitioner, as such he does not press the present appeal to the
aforesaid extent.

Further, learned counsel points out that in pursuance of acquisition of 3.987 acres of land
belonging to the petitioner-Trust petitioner Trust under the National Highways Act, 1956 read with
the provisions of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the 2013 Act'), the rights of the

sentences.text: Having heard learned learned counsel for the petitioner, at this stage, it may be pointed out here that before seeking any indulgence to the aforesaid extent, the 1 of 2 petitioner-Trust Trust should first approach respondent Nos.2 and 3 so as to seek enforcement of its rights for rehabilitation on and resettlement in terms of the provisions of 2013 Act by raising a demand within four weeks from today.
Thereafter the same be dealt with and disposed of by respondent Nos.2 and 3 in accordance with law within four weeks of its receipt.

[4]. At this stage, Mr. H.S. Gill, Advocate and Ms. Komal Sharma, D.A.G., Haryana, Haryana representing respondent Nos.2 and 3 respectively are requested to accept notice and appear on behalf of the said respondents,, in order to ensure the necessary compliance in the aforesaid context.
[5]. In such circumstances, circumstances the present writ petition is disposed of with the aforesaid liberty.
However, nothing stated hereinabove shall be construed as an expression/opinion on the rights righ s or merits of the case set up by the petitioner.
[6]. Pending application(s), if any shall also stand disposed of.
